title: What are You Saying? Using topic to Detect Financial Misreporting

scopes.description: Complete supplied 10-K topic workflow in z_log/main.sh: parsing, all four word-count dictionary branches, stopword generation, LDA, conversion, four-branch convergence comparisons, manual parameter sweeps and the final 10-Ks model. Paper-wide financial regressions and word-intrusion studies are not supplied as active entry stages.

requirements.description: Author-compatible raw SEC EDGAR 10-K filing text for years 1994–2012, arranged for the supplied parser and rolling five-year windows. The active main workflow parses 10-Ks; it does not read 10-K/A files.

issues.description: The package does not supply raw 10-K filings. Public SEC and local candidate routes exist, but complete author-compatible 1994–2012 coverage, source layout and filename mapping are not established. Parse.pyx reads PROC_PATH/Documents_Raw/10-K/<year>; the main.sh comment names a different Data_Files subpath.

Every active comparison/tuning branch reads 10-K_style_characteristics.csv by Filing, but no such table or Style_Parser source is packaged and its main.sh calls are commented out. Parse.pyx writes a differently named parse-characteristics table.

Active word-count branches require the three named Unix dictionaries, but none is included. Word_Counts.pyx compares each uppercase token plus newline against dictionary lines, so compatible newline-delimited uppercase wordlists can satisfy the contract; the exact author source/version is unresolved.

The tuning loops generate stopword files under 10-Ks and call LDA.py, LDA_Convert.py and Topic_Model_Compare2.py with 10-K. These consumers build paths from the passed filetype, so they do not read the immediately generated files. Final selected commands consistently use 10-Ks.

LDA.py iterates each batch index i but appends files[fed] for every item. Each batch repeats its first filing and omits the other file paths in that batch, preventing faithful topic estimation unless the index is corrected.

Topic_Model_Compare2 writes results beneath Stats/Topic_Test/5 for initial comparisons and Test/Stats/Topic_Test/5 for parameter sweeps. Neither folder is packaged, and the script does not create them.

Appendix A.2 says the simulations select 1,000 filings per year, while each tuning pass passes test=1000 to Stopword_Generator.pyx after it has assembled and shuffled a multi-year window list; the code truncates that per-window list to 1,000. The intended sampling unit is unresolved and must not be guessed.

Settings retains placeholder PROJECT_PATH and README directs users to configure it. A coherent host root and current directory are required because main.sh uses cd ../Code_pre while data paths derive from PROC_PATH.

review_notes: The target is the supplied topic-generation and manual-tuning workflow, including its active Topic_Model_Compare2 companion. The package 10-K_Info_fix.csv and outer GVKEY/restatement files are not read by this active closure. The in-package restate_data_2.csv is read and is a distinct compatible input. Paper-wide regressions, MTurk analysis and word-intrusion workflows are not supplied as active entry stages; AAER/Compustat/AuditAnalytics source data and GloVe resources are not mandatory for this selected code path.

No analysis-only scope is supported: no prepared LDA matrices/topics are packaged and the supplied target includes document preparation and every active dictionary/tuning branch. No author code was imported, compiled or run; no regressions, downloads or installations were attempted.

The README and main.sh mention NLTK Brown and Punkt, but the traced active closure contains no NLTK import or corpus lookup. Those notes are retained as documentation, not promoted to empirical inputs or additional mandatory resources.
